function: Joint design of the BS precoding matrix and discrete RIS phases (up to 2048 elements) to maximize sum spectral efficiency, learned with sequential multi-agent A2C (p. 2-3).
system: Indoor RIS-assisted MU-MISO downlink: BS with NT=16 antennas, K=3 users, reflecting RIS of 128-2048 elements with 1-2 bit phases, LOS blocked, wavelength 100 mm (p. 2, 4).
method: Sequential multi-agent A2C (CTDE): BS phase and amplitude actors, one actor per RIS sub-array, shared critic; MLPs with one hidden layer; reinforcement learning (p. 2-3).
data_channel: Own simulator: BS-RIS channel Rayleigh with exponential spatial correlation, RIS-user i.i.d. complex normal with angle-based correlation, LOS blocked, Gaussian CSI errors; no dataset (p. 2).
test_conditions: Each setting is its own case (RIS size, phase bits, uniform or clustered users, CSI error 0.1-0.6 I); no trained model is tested on unseen conditions (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: ZF and MMSE precoders with block coordinate descent RIS phases quantized to M bits; learned: single-agent A2C (p. 4).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bps/Hz) versus RIS size, cluster radius and CSI error; average reward learning curve; complexity expressions (p. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O: proposed O(N1 N2 (NR/NA)^2) after simplification; ZF/MMSE O(N3 N4 (NR/NA)); single-agent A2C O(N1 N2 NR^2); no runtime (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "modeled as an identical and independently distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh random variable"; custom correlated Rayleigh model with exponential correlation [10], no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "the average reward for each case gradually converges as the episode number increases"; each RIS size, correlation and CSI-error setting is its own case, and no model trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 4: "We adopt the zero-forcing (ZF), minimum mean square error (MMSE), and single-agent A2C algorithms as the benchmarks"; ZF and MMSE are non-learned, but single-agent A2C is the proposed method without the multi-agent split, and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "The computational complexity of the proposed algorithm can be summarized as" O(N1 N2((K NT)^2 + (NR/NA)^2 + (K NT + NR/NA)^2 + K NT NR + K^2 NT)), simplified to O(N1 N2 (NR/NA)^2).
q5_support: p. 4: "We first give the parameter settings for the proposed algorithm and the ZF algorithm in Table I"; own simulator, no code or data link or DOI, no public dataset.
notes: Area 3: joint BS precoder and RIS phases for MU-MISO, no sensing. q3 is borderline: the only learned comparator, single-agent A2C, has complexity O(N1 N2 NR^2) (p. 4), which is the proposed expression O(N1 N2 (NR/NA)^2) with NA = 1, so it is treated as an ablation; ZF and MMSE are the non-learned baselines. Table I was read from the page image (p. 4).
